faqs.question: What is the ALPHA II Compact FT-IR Spectrometer used for?
faqs.answer: The ALPHA II identifies, quantifies, and verifies materials, from raw ingredients to finished products, across applications including polymers, pharmaceuticals, food, environmental testing, and forensic drug analysis.

faqs.question: How long does a measurement take?
faqs.answer: Bruker states that a full workflow, from selection to result, takes under a minute using OPUS TOUCH.

faqs.question: Is the ALPHA II suitable for a regulated laboratory?
faqs.answer: Yes. It offers full 21 CFR Part 11 compliance, follows the ALCOA+ principle, and includes secure user profiles with complete audit trails. Bruker also offers an ISO 17025 support package for laboratories pursuing accreditation.

faqs.question: Does the ALPHA II require extensive operator training?
faqs.answer: No. Guided workflows and built-in tutorial videos are designed to let a new operator work independently after a short introduction.

faqs.question: What is OPUS TOUCH?
faqs.answer: OPUS TOUCH is the ALPHA II's touch-screen software interface. It guides users through method selection, measurement, and report generation.

faqs.question: Can the ALPHA II monitor a chemical reaction in real time?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the optional INSITU-ATR module, which tracks reaction progress, intermediates, and endpoints directly in the reaction vessel using a diamond crystal probe.

faqs.question: Can the ALPHA II analyze soil samples?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the dedicated Soil Analyzer configuration, which reports organic carbon, texture, pH, carbonates, and other parameters from a single measurement.

faqs.question: What is included with the ALPHA II?
faqs.answer: The base solution includes OPUS TOUCH software and the core optical components. Sampling accessories and application-specific modules, such as INSITU-ATR or the Soil Analyzer configuration, are confirmed separately based on your application.

faqs.question: What is the MOBILE-IR II FT-IR Spectrometer used for?
faqs.answer: The MOBILE-IR II is a portable FT-IR spectrometer used for field identification of materials, including forensic drug testing, customs screening, warehouse quality control, and polymer sorting.

faqs.question: How is this different from a benchtop FT-IR spectrometer?
faqs.answer: It's built to work off-grid and in harsh environments, with IP65 enclosure protection and an IP67 carry case, while its TE-MCT detector halves measurement time and doubles signal-to-noise ratio compared to a standard DTGS detector.

faqs.question: Does portability mean a compromise in performance?
faqs.answer: No. Bruker states the TE-MCT detector outperforms a standard DTGS detector on both speed and signal-to-noise ratio, so field use doesn't come at the cost of measurement quality.

faqs.question: How much training does an operator need?
faqs.answer: OPUS TOUCH is stated to require about 10 minutes of training to operate.

faqs.question: How does the MOBILE-IR II connect to other systems?
faqs.answer: Through Wi-Fi, Ethernet, cloud, or USB, with data transfer to LIMS or MES systems via MS SQL.

faqs.question: What sampling accessory does it use?
faqs.answer: A heatable diamond ATR crystal with a sample trough, for rapid liquid evaporation and temperature experiments. A non-heatable flat ATR plate is also available for larger flat samples.

faqs.question: Does it run without mains power?
faqs.answer: Yes. An internal high-capacity battery powers off-grid and in-field operation, with a charge indicator at 100, 75, 50, and 25 percent.

faqs.question: Is the MOBILE-IR II suitable for regulated laboratory use?
faqs.answer: Bruker's documentation for this solution does not state 21 CFR Part 11 or ISO 17025 compliance. For a regulated lab environment, the benchtop ALPHA II is built around that requirement.

sections.title: Field Performance and Detector Advantage
sections.tabSummary: What the TE-MCT detector actually buys you
body: The detector is what separates a field spectrometer that merely survives outdoors from one that performs there.

A standard DTGS detector works, but it's slower and less sensitive than it needs to be once external conditions start interfering, which is exactly what a warehouse floor or a construction site does. The TE-MCT detector in the MOBILE-IR II is cooled thermoelectrically rather than with liquid nitrogen, and Bruker states it halves measurement time and doubles signal-to-noise ratio against a standard DTGS detector, with the added benefit of greater spectral stability against those external influences.

rows: Fast turnaround during a raid or inspection
Half the measurement time of a DTGS-based system
Reliable readings in a noisy or vibrating environment
Improved spectral stability against external interference
No liquid nitrogen supply chain in the field
Confidence in a borderline or trace-level result

cta.title: Get the MOBILE-IR II FT-IR Spectrometer in India from Inkarp
cta.subheading: Authorized distributor and service provider. Demonstration, installation, AMC, and genuine spare parts.
cta.description: The MOBILE-IR II brings lab-grade FT-IR into the field, with a detector that halves measurement time and doubles signal-to-noise ratio, and a build rated for dust, water jets, and off-grid power. Tell us your deployment environment, and Inkarp will confirm the right configuration.
cta.label: Request Quote

longForm.heroHook: Half the measurement time. Double the signal. Even in the field.
heroParagraphs: A portable spectrometer usually means a compromise. Less power, slower results, or both.
The MOBILE-IR II doesn't make that trade. Its cryogen-free detector halves measurement time and doubles signal-to-noise ratio compared to a standard DTGS detector.
It runs on an internal battery, off the grid, wherever the sample is. IP65 protection keeps out dust and water jets. The carry case is rated IP67.
A heatable diamond ATR crystal evaporates liquids and runs temperature experiments on the spot. OPUS TOUCH software needs about 10 minutes of training to operate.
Connect however your work requires. Wi-Fi, Ethernet, cloud, or USB.
longForm.statsIntro: The quick stats of the MOBILE-IR II FT-IR Spectrometer cover its detector advantage, ruggedness, power, and connectivity.
